app: Live Geometry (worlds: Matt's Reality / Ready Security Services Map 1 / Base Geometry Reality)

sphere.angles: degrees, bearings clockwise from true north

equations.R: R = 6,371,000 m (all renderers). Distance read-outs in some places use 6,371 km or 6,371.0088 km (<=1.4 ppm). Earth = sphere, heights h are radial.
equations.unit vector: v(lat,lon) = (cos lat cos lon, cos lat sin lon, sin lat); +X=(0,0), +Y=(0,90E), +Z=North Pole
equations.inverse: lat = asin(Pz/|P|), lon = atan2(Py, Px), h = |P| - R
equations.ENU basis at (lat0,lon0): E = (-sin lon0, cos lon0, 0); N = (-sin lat0 cos lon0, -sin lat0 sin lon0, cos lat0); U = v(lat0,lon0); enu = (E.(P-P0), N.(P-P0), U.(P-P0))
equations.scene axes: Three.js: x = E, y = U, z = -N (y-up, right-handed). index.html world group: metres*1e-3 (km); local group: metres; quest: metres from HOME (default Ready Athletics or the manual location)
equations.flat local map (figures, landmark pillar: x = (lon-lon0)*111320*cos(lat0), z = -(lat-lat0)*111320, y = -1.6 m (floor); lat0/lon0 = viewer position rounded to 0.001 deg. Exact = ENU above. Error: scale +0.11% (111320 vs R*pi/180 = 111194.9 m/deg) and no drop; 2.8 m at Cappy's seen from Ready Athletics (2.4 km), 11.7 m at 10 km.
equations.great-circle distance (haversine): d = 2R asin( sqrt( sin^2(dlat/2) + cos lat1 cos lat2 sin^2(dlon/2) ) )
equations.initial bearing: theta = atan2( sin dlon cos lat2, cos lat1 sin lat2 - sin lat1 cos lat2 cos dlon ) (clockwise from north)
equations.destination: delta = d/R; lat2 = asin(sin lat1 cos delta + cos lat1 sin delta cos theta); lon2 = lon1 + atan2(sin theta sin delta cos lat1, cos delta - sin lat1 sin lat2)
equations.direction vector: d_theta = cos theta N + sin theta E (unit tangent at v)
equations.great circle: plane through Earth centre {p : p.n = 0}; n = v x d_theta (through v heading theta) or n = (v1 x v2)/|v1 x v2| (through two points)
equations.point on great circle: p(s) = cos s v + sin s d_theta, s = arc/R in radians, s in [0, 2pi)
equations.small circle: centre c, ground radius r: {p : p.c = cos rho}, rho = r/R; p(t) = cos rho c + sin rho (cos t N + sin t E). App draws a flat tangent-plane circle of radius r (difference: sagitta r^2/2R = 7 mm at 300 m).
equations.wedge index (any point on Earth): k = floor( ((theta(c->p) - 0) mod 360) / 30 ), k = 0..11; equivalently lune test p.n(30k) < 0 and p.n(30k+30) > 0 with n(theta) = v x d_theta, n(theta+180) = -n(theta)
equations.spherical polygon area: A = R^2 |sum_i 2 atan2( c.(a_i x a_i+1), 1 + c.a_i + a_i.a_i+1 + a_i+1.c )|, c = normalised vertex mean (vertices joined by great-circle arcs)
equations.point in spherical polygon: ray-cast along a great circle from p to a point known outside; or (small polygons) flat test in ENU/azimuthal-equidistant at the polygon centre
equations.horizon: distance to the geometric horizon for eye height h: d = sqrt(2Rh + h^2) (h = 1.6 m -> 4,515 m; 1.8 m -> 4,789 m; 100 m -> 35.7 km). Ground drop at arc s: R(1 - cos(s/R)) ~ s^2/2R (1 km 7.8 cm, 10 km 7.85 m, 110 km 950 m).
equations.past the horizon: every world object is placed at its TRUE ENU position (through the planet, negative elevation), drawn with depth test off so it shows through the ground; world great circles skip points < 60 km from the viewer (the 110 km ground half-lines own the near part); Quest projects world points to a 3 km shell along the true direction (direction and angular size preserved). Edge-of-Earth markers sit 90 deg of arc away (10,007.5 km): chord R*sqrt2 = 9,010 km, elevation -45 deg. Antipode: chord 2R = 12,742 km, elevation -90 deg.
equations.azimuthal-equidistant (continent triangu: c = acos(sin lat0 sin lat + cos lat0 cos lat cos dlon); k = c/sin c; x = k cos lat sin dlon R, y = k (cos lat0 sin lat - sin lat0 cos lat cos dlon) R; earcut there, triangles subdivided to <= 150-250 km, each vertex placed back on the sphere

Face 0.70 x 1.67 m (aspect .419) vs image 432x1024 (aspect .422): no crop, <1% stretch.

encoding: GeoJSON coordinates are [lon,lat] (RFC 7946); the app JSON files (trails/streets/sheridan/shore/continents/landmass/pillars-as-fields) use [lat,lon]. Decimal degrees, 7 decimals (~1.1 cm). Rings closed (first==last). Consecutive vertices are joined by great-circle arcs (slerp). .f32 = little-endian float32 xyz unit vectors (~0.6 m precision; use float64 from the GeoJSON for sub-metre work).
